modules.method: Tier 1, static: distribute project peak-hour vehicle trips onto approaches using access positions and shortest paths on the OSM network; add background volumes (screenline growth and hourly shape as context); compute v/c per movement from saturation flow and green split and delay with HCM-style terms using user timings; classify delay with the FHWA/HCM bands as descriptive colours and report the lane-group v/c override separately (expert-stated, unverified). Report pedestrian maximum wait (cycle minus walk interval) beside vehicle delay. Tier 2, simulation (roadmap): export network and demand to SUMO (netconvert) or UXsim and read edge delays and queues from detectors, with-project versus without-project. A mode-priority check reads pedestrian bands from P09-M04 and flags mitigation that trades pedestrian comfort for vehicle delay. The 15-minute PHF is an explicit input. Placeholder signal data are labelled.
modules.human_judgment: How much vehicle delay to accept against pedestrian, cycle and transit priority, whether to propose street changes, how to narrate impact in the policy reflection, and whether assumed signal timings are credible.
modules.limits: City data are link-only intersection counts (2020) and 2004-2013 counters in a legacy tool; screenline counts are regional and 2011/2017. No signal timings or lane widths. HCM is paywalled, so delay formulas are generic and HCM 2000 bands may differ from later editions. The site is hypothetical, so trips are scenario inputs. Microsimulation needs calibration; results are comparative and not a traffic impact study.

flags.claim: Downtown Vancouver, or any Vancouver site, must provide a minimum number of off-street parking spaces.
flags.correction: No minimum parking applies for any use citywide since 30 June 2024; the downtown peninsula was exempt from 2018. Accessible, visitor, bicycle and loading spaces are still required.
flags.detail: Sources S01 and S02 (opened) agree. The Province's TOA rules also bar required residential parking near rapid transit (S24). The tool must never score a parking shortfall as a deficiency.

flags.claim: The 2023 Trip Diary weekday shares for CBD sub-regions 21 and 22 are the right default mode split for all trips the tower generates (office, retail, hotel, residential).
flags.correction: Use residence-based shares for residential trips and destination-based shares (trips ending in the CBD: Census place-of-work, City cordon counts or a dashboard destination filter) for attraction uses. Store basis, sample size and confidence interval with each loaded share and flag attraction runs on a residence-based share (r2: watermark, not block).
flags.detail: The survey recruits and weights households by residence sub-area (S15 weighting exhibit uses household and person controls by sub seed; sub-regions 21 and 22 have household sample targets of a few hundred each). The shares therefore describe trips by CBD residents, not workers and visitors arriving from across the region. Evidence: S15 (opened, text extracted); S16 lists no destination-based product.

flags.claim: TfL Pedestrian Comfort Level bands are verified thresholds for peak-minute flows in below-grade station passages, with B+ (11 ppmm or less) good and 18 ppmm or more bad for all area types.
flags.correction: Use TfL only for street footways and crossings, on peak-hour flow (people per hour / 60 / clear width), against the Figure 9 acceptability table by area type. Use station methods (TCQSM chapter 10 walkway and queuing scales) for passages, stairs and fare lines. Status: team_assumption.
flags.detail: S17 (opened, text extracted): scope is footways and crossings; ppmm is people per hour divided by 60 and by clear width, calculated for average, peak-hour and Average of Maximum Activity flows. Multiplying hourly flow by a platoon factor and reading hour-average bands double-counts peaking. [r2 note: the round-1 wording here about the C+ floor and the cell-level Figure 9 reading was superseded by the r2 flag on Figure 9; C+ is the limit on the vitality exception, not a general fail line.]

flags.claim: Queue area per person of 1.4 m2 or more is Fruin LOS A-C and below 0.9 m2 is LOS E-F at stairs and fare lines.
flags.correction: 1.4 and 0.9 m2 per person are walkway-scale boundaries (C/D and D/E). Queues use a separate queuing-area scale (reviewer: A 1.2 or more, B 0.9-1.2, C 0.7-0.9, D 0.3-0.7, E 0.2-0.3, F under 0.2 m2 per person). Keep both scales and cite the exhibit once read.
flags.detail: Reviewer expert knowledge of Fruin (1971) as reproduced in TCQSM 3rd ed. ch.10. The primary copy could not be opened (S44 reader page has no table text, re-tried in r2; the PDF exceeds the fetch size limit), so both scales stay unverified and bounds such as 0.65 versus 0.7 m2 may differ by edition.

flags.claim: Peak headways relevant to the station are Expo 2-5 min, Millennium 3-4 min and Canada 6 min.
flags.correction: For a CBD station use the Expo trunk (about 2-3 min combined) and the Canada Line trunk (about 3 min combined), read from GTFS for the actual station. The Millennium Line terminates at VCC-Clark and is excluded.
flags.detail: S23 (re-opened): Expo 2-5 min is the line's own frequency and 2-3 min combined on shared track; Millennium runs VCC-Clark to Lafarge Lake-Douglas and is not shown serving Waterfront since 2016; Canada Line 6 min is its own branch frequency and 3 min combined on the trunk. [r2 note: the correction above was itself incomplete; see the r2 flag on combining both trunks at one station.]

flags.claim: FHWA Table 3-2 gives v/c bands of under 0.85 stable, 0.85-1.00 near capacity and over 1.00 oversaturated.
flags.correction: Cite Table 3-2 exactly: under 0.85, 0.85-0.95 near capacity, 0.95-1.00 unstable flow, over 1.00 demand exceeds capacity. The single 0.85-1.00 band is from section 3.3.5. Add the reviewer-stated LOS F override for lane-group v/c above 1.0 (later HCM editions; unverified) and label the method HCM-style.
flags.detail: S18 re-opened (r1 and r2): Table 3-2 lists under 0.85, 0.85-0.95, 0.95-1.00 and over 1.00 (HCM 2000 Quick Estimation Method). The page does not map v/c above 1.0 to LOS F; Table 3-3 assigns LOS F by delay above 80 s only.

flags.claim: VTPI TDM reduction ranges (4-20%, about 15%, 34-37%, 35%) are verified thresholds for claimed reductions at a downtown Vancouver tower.
flags.correction: Treat them as team-applied evidence ranges with an 'evidence context: US metro / predicted' label on each value.
flags.detail: S19 re-opened: the 35% and 20% figures are Ewing 1993 Sacramento model predictions; 34-37% is measured against ITE average trip rates in Minneapolis-St Paul (Spack and Finkelstein 2014); 4-20% is Rye and Boarnet worksite programmes; 15% versus 7% is a four-metro US survey. [r2 note: the round-1 remedy of scaling these by k = site auto share / evidence auto share was itself false; see the r2 flag.]

flags.claim: ITE trip rates do not consider location, so local survey data are the only option for downtown sites.
flags.correction: ITE is paywalled but, per the reviewer, recent editions classify data by site setting (including Center City Core and Dense Multi-Use Urban) and report person trips; use as an optional cross-check where a user holds a licence.
flags.detail: S46 (Wikipedia) repeats the older wording. The reviewer states the setting categories from practitioner knowledge; ITE pages could not be opened (404, S54), so this correction is unverified.

flags.claim: Published TDM reductions should be scaled down for a low-auto CBD site by k = site auto share / evidence auto share (capped at 1), so a CBD site gets a smaller claim.
flags.correction: Select the evidence row by context (Ewing CBD and near-station columns, labelled as predictions). Keep k only as an optional sensitivity marked team assumption. Bound claims by an absolute floor at the lowest same-basis observed CBD share loaded in M01.
flags.detail: S19 re-opened in round 2: Ewing 1993 Table 1 gives a 100% transit/rideshare subsidy at 35% for the CBD, 25% within 660 ft of a transit station and 10% elsewhere (50% subsidy: 20%, 15%, 10%), and the page states 'Proximity to quality transit service tends to increase program effectiveness.' The k rule shrinks claims exactly where the source predicts larger effects; it was an unsourced rule presented as a correction in round 1.

flags.claim: On street footways, C+ (18 ppmm) is the fail line for every TfL area type, B- (15-17 ppmm) is only 'at risk', and B+ or better is the good level for every area type.
flags.correction: Use the cell-level Figure 9 lookup by area type and by peak versus Average of Maximum, with the recommended minimum B+ (Figure 8) as the good line. C+ is the limit on a documented vitality exception (p.12), not the general fail line. Add the Tourist Attraction area type, the crossing-arm check (B- recommended, 15-18 ppmm) and the footway total-width minima (2.9, 4.2, 5.3 m).
flags.detail: S17 p.12: vitality such as cafe seating may justify a lower level, 'not lower than C+ at peak'. Figure 9 (p.14): the text layer is garbled, so round 2 decoded the cells from the page's vector fills (four fills, each printed label lies inside its own fill). Decoded: High Street and Tourist Attraction - comfortable to B+, acceptable B, at risk B-, unacceptable C+ and worse; Residential - acceptable B and B-, at risk C+ at peak, unacceptable beyond; Office and Retail and Transport Interchange - comfortable to B, acceptable B- and C+, at risk C row at peak, unacceptable D and E. The critic's text-based reading differs (B at risk for Office and Retail, Residential and Transport Interchange; Tourist B+ at risk and B unacceptable). Both readings agree that one 11/18 pair for all area types is wrong. Cells stay unverified until two people confirm them against the PDF image.

flags.claim: For the neighbouring station, use the Expo trunk (2-3 min) and the Canada Line trunk (about 3 min) headways combined.
flags.correction: Require a proxy-station choice and load only that station's lines from GTFS; combine trunks only at Waterfront; treat a new-station scenario as user-entered with per-line train capacity entered by the user.
flags.detail: S23 and S61 (opened): Waterfront is the only station where the Canada Line directly connects with the Expo Line; Vancouver City Centre is a Canada Line station with an unofficial walking transfer to Granville. S62 lists Burrard, Granville and Stadium-Chinatown as Expo-only. Combining both trunks elsewhere overstates frequency and understates platoon size.

flags.claim: No cordon or screenline data exist, so auto occupancy, background volumes and truck shares are unsourced presets.
flags.correction: Use TransLink screenline products as team-applied defaults: 2011 report (auto occupancy 1.24 regional, 1.17 AM peak, 1.25 CBD screenline; trucks about 6%), 2017 summary (trucks about 4%, CBD volume trend). They are vehicle counts at screenlines, through trips included, not site rates. The 2014 truck survey and 2023 screenline dashboard were not readable.
flags.detail: S16 lists the 2023 Screenline Survey dashboard, earlier reports and the 2014 Truck Classification and Dangerous Goods Survey; S56 and S57 were opened and extracted in round 2. The 2017 summary carries classification only, not occupancy; the 2011 report carries occupancy. S31 shows no City cordon or pedestrian-count dataset, but the 2011 report has a few manual downtown pedestrian counts.

flags.claim: Downtown maximum for non-residential parking is 1 space per 115 m2 GFA (s.4.2.5).
flags.detail: Seen only in a search-engine extract of the June 2026 Section 4, which could not be opened (bot challenge). Whether the hypothetical VTC block falls inside the by-law's Downtown area is also unconfirmed. A residential maximum row exists in the schema, unpopulated.

flags.claim: Loading rules: Class A, B and C requirements by use and GFA, and bay dimensions (Class B 8.5 x 3.0 x 3.8 m in 2012; 10.2 x 3.4 m in a May 2026 extract).
flags.detail: Section 5 and the Design Supplement could not be opened (Section 5 re-tried, HTTP 403; the consolidated by-law PDF also 403 in round 2). The 1988 supplement has a 'superseded' copy. The 2003 and 2012 residential thresholds (none under 100 dwellings) are old. Load the current table by hand through the rule pack.

flags.claim: Bicycle parking rates (dwelling 1.5/2.5/3 per unit by size; office 1 per 170 m2; retail 1 per 340 m2; hotel 1 per 30 units; Class B minima).
flags.detail: Only from a vendor's partial list (S13). A second vendor page (no longer kept as a source) claims 1.25 per dwelling, and Memon (S12, opened) reports Council approved 1.25 per unit and 1 per 500 m2 commercial in 2008. The Feb 2026 Section 6 was not opened. Treat all as placeholders until the official table is loaded.

flags.claim: City of Vancouver sustainable-mode target of two-thirds of trips and any newer 2050 target.
flags.detail: Transportation 2040, the climate plan and the Vancouver Plan were not opened (vancouver.ca returns HTTP 403). The reviewer notes the target is city-wide and may have a 2030 year in a later plan. The 1997 plan targets in Memon 2009 are historical. Shown as context, not pass/fail.

flags.claim: 2023 Trip Diary mode shares for CBD sub-regions 21 and 22.
flags.detail: The technical report (opened) contains no results; shares exist only in TransLink's Tableau dashboard (S16), are residence-based, and whether a destination filter exists is unconfirmed (Tableau pages return no readable text to fetch). Users must read and enter values with basis, sample size and date accessed.

flags.claim: Queuing-area and walkway LOS scales (Fruin) used for stair, fare-line and passage checks.
flags.detail: Reviewer-supplied boundaries (walkway C/D 1.4 and D/E 0.9 m2 per person; queuing A 1.2 or more through F under 0.2) are not read from a primary copy. TCQSM chapter 10 (S44) returned no table text. Stair, escalator and fare-gate throughputs remain unsourced. Keep unverified until read.

flags.claim: The VTC site lies inside a Provincial Transit-Oriented Area.
flags.detail: The TOA page (S24) says 104 areas exist within 800 m of rapid transit, but Vancouver's list was not read, and the site is hypothetical. If it applies, residential parking cannot be required there.

flags.claim: The 1997 Higher Buildings Policy still governs tall-building criteria and has not been replaced by the Review.
flags.detail: The Shape Your City page (S47, opened) says the City is reviewing the policy, with Phase 1 in spring-summer 2026 and adoption expected spring 2027, so the 1997 policy has not been replaced. The policy PDF (S42) returned HTTP 403, the Review's engagement document named in the brief was dropped as a source (not opened), and the page names no transportation criteria. Parking By-law No. 6059 remains the governing instrument for parking, loading and bicycle spaces.

flags.claim: City of Vancouver TDM requirement for developments after the June 2024 parking-minimum removal.
flags.detail: Storeys (S02, opened) reports the TDM policy 'is tied to the minimum parking requirements, which now no longer exist' and staff intend to lower financial expectations in Downtown, Broadway Plan area and TOAs. The City bulletin was not opened; a c. 2021 City memo (no longer kept as a source) predates the change, so the TDM-variance logic may be superseded. Carried as a rule row 'unverified pending the City bulletin'.

flags.claim: Emergency egress criteria (NFPA 130 or the authority's rail-station rules) may govern passage and stair width in the station connection regardless of comfort.
flags.detail: Reviewer statement; NFPA 130 (S52) page returned only its title. M03 withholds green width badges and labels outputs 'comfort only, not egress-compliant' until an egress record from SYST is attached.

flags.claim: EV-charging and car-share provisions in the Parking By-law rule pack.
flags.detail: The reviewer said Memon documents EV outlets in the by-law. Memon (S12, opened) actually reports car-share requirements and electrical outlets for electric-assisted bicycles in the by-law, with EV-car outlets described as voluntary or project-specific (East Fraserlands 20%). Current EV rules may sit in the Vancouver Building By-law; rows are loaded as unverified.

flags.claim: TfL Figure 9 cell ratings by area type, as decoded in round 2 from the page's vector fills.
flags.detail: The PDF text layer is garbled; the decode matches every printed label to its fill colour (S17 p.14) and is consistent with the figure's own notes on Average of Maximum Activity, but it has not been checked against a rendered image, and it disagrees with the critic's reading for Office and Retail, Residential, Tourist Attraction and Transport Interchange. The row printed 'C-' may stand for the C and C- bands (21-26 ppmm). Two-person visual confirmation is due 31 Oct; until then the tool shows 'cells unconfirmed' and always applies the B+ minimum.

flags.claim: TransLink TSPR station values (2025 weekday averages and 2023 hourly alightings and boardings) as baselines for station-patron demand.
flags.detail: S58 CSV headers (AvgStationBrdgs_MF and so on) were read, but the page defines no column meanings or segment codes, so 'MF' as weekday average boardings is inferred from the names. Hourly rows were read for 2023 only (Burrard, Granville); 2025 hourly rows were not reached in the 640,000-character file.

flags.claim: Lane right-of-way default of 6.1 m (20 ft) for City lanes.
flags.detail: S48 records carry text widths with no unit; unmarked values 66, 20, 33, 80, 73 and metric values marked '(m)'. Within 1.5 km of Burrard and Georgia, 198 records read 20 and 259 read 66, which fits feet (lane and street) but the unit is inferred. Right-of-way is not paved width.

flags.claim: Line capacity references (Canada Line 15,000 pphpd RFP requirement, 334/400 per two-car train; Expo 12,000 to 19,400 pphpd, Mark V 672/1,207).
flags.detail: From Wikipedia pages S61 and S62 (secondary); TransLink train loads and platform capacities were not found. The page lists Expo capacities of 25,700 with five-car Mark II trains as a potential figure. Users must replace them with TransLink data.

flags.claim: HCM-style pedestrian signal delay and LOS thresholds for crossings.
flags.detail: FHWA chapter 3 (S18) places pedestrian LOS outside its scope, so only arithmetic maximum wait (cycle length minus walk interval) is reported; the HCM average pedestrian delay formula and bands were not opened.

flags.claim: Whether the Parking By-law requires passenger loading spaces and at what rate.
flags.detail: No extract captured a passenger-loading clause; a reviewer reports Section 5 includes passenger-space rows by use including hotels. M02 carries passenger-space row types as 'unverified - load from Section 5', and M05 sizes kerb bays as the larger of by-law rows and queue-model demand.

flags.claim: Destination-based mode shares for office, retail, hotel and civic attraction trips to the CBD.
flags.detail: Candidate sources: Statistics Canada 2016 and 2021 place-of-work tables (S51, HTTP 403, table not identified; 2021 COVID-affected), City downtown cordon counts (cited in S12; no open dataset found), a TransLink dashboard destination filter (unconfirmed; Tableau unreadable by fetch). Due 7 Nov by data sprint; until then M01 runs scenario shares watermarked 'unsourced scenario'.

flags.claim: Whether the 2023 Screenline Survey dashboard reports auto occupancy and pedestrian counts.
flags.detail: S16 lists the dashboard but Tableau pages return no readable text. The 2011 report (S56) has occupancy; the 2017 summary (S57) does not.

flags.claim: Servicing, waste and entry presets: truck arrival rates, dwell times, waste generation, container sizes, screening rates, arrival peaking, utilisation and wait thresholds.
flags.detail: No sourced Vancouver values were found. All appear as editable team-assumption badges and become verified only when a user attaches a source. M06 is experimental and shows relative comparisons only.

flags.claim: TfL Pedestrian Comfort Levels (London footways, 2010) are an acceptable threshold system for Vancouver street footways and crossings, mapped to TfL area types.
flags.detail: B+ as the recommended minimum and the Figure 9 acceptability grid are TfL rules, not City of Vancouver standards. The street-class to area-type mapping (arterial to Office and Retail, high street to High Street, station-entry footways to Transport Interchange, plaza, civic frontage and event days to Tourist Attraction) is a team choice. Not used for station passages. Teams may substitute another comfort scale.

flags.claim: LOS D is the acceptable level for vehicle delay at downtown intersections.
flags.detail: LOS delay bands are sourced (S18) but acceptability is a choice. The City ranks walking, cycling and transit above cars, so round 2 shows vehicle LOS as descriptive context with no pass/fail badge and reports pedestrian crossing wait beside it.

flags.claim: Internal capture is OFF by default in CBD mode and station-entrance choice uses shortest walking time.
flags.detail: Tool design choices to avoid double-discounting trips already in the zone shares (reviewer) and to avoid using mode-choice elasticities for entrance choice. Optional logit scale and NCHRP 684 pair rates are user entries.

flags.claim: Screenline auto occupancy (1.24 regional, 1.17 AM peak, 1.25 CBD screenline, 2011) is an acceptable default for tower person-trips.
flags.detail: S56 counts vehicles crossing screenlines (through trips included, longer-distance commuting), in 2011. Applicability to a downtown tower's mixed trips is a team choice; values remain editable.

flags.claim: A proxy station stands in for the hypothetical neighbouring station, and route directness is judged relative to a without-passage case.
flags.detail: The brief's station is hypothetical, so any real station's lines, headways and flows are proxies (team-applied). Route directness has no sourced pass/fail threshold; the relative test is a design choice (S60 gives only a walking-share association).

unresolved_relationships: Destination-based CBD mode shares by purpose (office, retail, hotel, civic): no loaded source; Census place-of-work 2016 and 2021 tables not identified or opened, TransLink dashboards unreadable by fetch; dated sprint 7 Nov, scenario fallback until then.
Visitor and event-day shares for cultural, civic and public uses (BC Place, Entertainment District): no sourced rates.
Share of station flow captured by a new secondary entrance versus walking time and entrance count: no source; the VTPI elasticities describe mode choice, not entrance choice.
Egress width criteria (NFPA 130 or authority rules) for the below-grade connection versus comfort width: standard not opened.
Stair, escalator, lift and fare-gate throughput versus width, and the Fruin walkway and queuing exhibit values: TCQSM chapter 10 returned no text (re-tried in round 2).
Platform storage and train-load limits for the proxy station: no TransLink train-load or platform-area source; line capacities are secondary (Wikipedia).
